title: On the survival of dark matter spikes: Stellar and compact-object perturbations
summary: Establishing realistic expectations for the dark matter (DM) distribution near a supermassive black hole (BH) is essential for assessing environmental imprints on gravitational wave (GW) signals. Using the Galactic Center as an observationally constrained case study, we investigate the evolution of DM density spikes under gravitational perturbations from the nuclear stellar and black hole populations surrounding the central BH. We find that scattering of DM particles by the nuclear star cluster depletes the DM distribution at radii $r \sim 10^{-1}~\mathrm{pc}$, far outside the region where the relevant GW signals are produced. At smaller radii, at $r \sim 10^{-3}~\mathrm{pc}$, the closest known stellar perturbers, S2 and S38, induce only negligible changes to the density profile. At still smaller radii, where no stellar perturbers are currently known, we assess the cumulative impact of past EMRIs by modelling successive mergers with stellar-mass BHs of mass $\sim10~\mathrm{M}_\odot$, in numbers consistent with the expected rate over $10~\mathrm{Gyr}$. We find that these events do not erase the central overdensity, reducing the density only to approximately $82 \%$ of its initial value at $r \lesssim 10^{-5}~\mathrm{pc}$. Our results indicate that, at least at the Galactic Center, DM overdensities around the central BH are expected to remain largely intact under stellar perturbations and plausible stellar-BH merger histories.

AI.tldr: Using the Galactic Center as a case study, this paper shows that DM density spikes around a supermassive BH remain largely intact despite gravitational perturbations from nuclear star clusters (depleting at ~0.1 pc), nearby stellar orbits (negligible at ~10⁻³ pc), and past EMRIs (density reduced only to ~82% at ≲10⁻⁵ pc), indicating that DM overdensities at the Galactic Center survive under realistic astrophysical conditions.
AI.motivation: Establishing realistic expectations for the DM distribution near a supermassive BH is essential for assessing environmental imprints on gravitational wave signals.
AI.method: Using the Galactic Center as an observationally constrained case study, the authors investigate the evolution of DM density spikes under gravitational perturbations from the nuclear stellar cluster and stellar-mass BH mergers (EMRIs), modeled over 10 Gyr.
AI.result: Scattering by the nuclear star cluster depletes DM at r ~ 0.1 pc; the closest stellar perturbers S2 and S38 cause negligible changes at r ~ 10⁻³ pc; cumulative past EMRIs reduce density only to ~82% of its initial value at r ≲ 10⁻⁵ pc.
AI.conclusion: DM overdensities around the central BH at the Galactic Center are expected to remain largely intact under stellar perturbations and plausible stellar-BH merger histories.

title: Turbulence in the multi-phase circumgalactic medium: bridging TNG50 and idealized kpc-scale simulations
comment: To be submitted to the Open Journal of Astrophysics, comments welcome
summary: The circumgalactic medium (CGM) is the extended multi-phase gaseous halo surrounding a galaxy. To study how its dynamics are shaped by the interplay of radiative cooling and turbulence, we first turn to the TNG50 cosmological magnetohydrodynamical simulation. We analyze the turbulent properties of the CGM of Milky Way-like galaxies at z=0, using a multi-scale filtering technique. We find that the CGM hosts predominantly subsonic flows with Mach number ~ 0.1 - 0.7 that are roughly balanced between compressive and solenoidal components with b = M_comp / M_tot ~ 0.3 - 0.6. We then use these physically motivated properties of turbulent CGM media to set the initial conditions and driving parameters for idealized, turbulent box simulations. These represent ~ 1 kpc^3 volumes of the CGM, but reach resolutions higher than available in cosmological volumes such as TNG50. To do so, we implement a turbulent driving algorithm into the AREPO code based on random but smoothly time-fluctuating acceleration fields, and then run a suite of turbulent boxes across the parameter space, including a model for metal-line radiative cooling. Using these simulations, we study how turbulence seeds density fluctuations that trigger thermal instability and promotes mixing between hot and cold phases, depending on the relative timescales of cooling and mixing. The abundance and evolution of cold ~10^4 K gas depends strongly on the strength of turbulence and the efficiency of cooling.

AI.tldr: The study analyzes turbulent properties of the CGM in Milky Way-like galaxies using TNG50 simulations, then uses those properties to set up idealized turbulent box simulations with radiative cooling to study how turbulence seeds density fluctuations, triggers thermal instability, and promotes mixing between hot and cold gas phases.
AI.motivation: To understand how the dynamics of the circumgalactic medium (CGM) are shaped by the interplay between radiative cooling and turbulence.
AI.method: First, turbulent properties of the CGM in Milky Way-like galaxies at z=0 are analyzed using TNG50 cosmological magnetohydrodynamical simulations with a multi-scale filtering technique. Then, physically motivated turbulent box simulations (~1 kpc^3 volumes) are run using the AREPO code with a turbulent driving algorithm based on random, smoothly time-fluctuating acceleration fields, incorporating metal-line radiative cooling across a parameter space.
AI.result: The CGM hosts predominantly subsonic flows (Mach ~0.1-0.7) with a balance between compressive and solenoidal components (b ~0.3-0.6). The abundance and evolution of cold ~10^4 K gas depends strongly on turbulence strength and cooling efficiency.
AI.conclusion: Turbulence seeds density fluctuations that trigger thermal instability and promote mixing between hot and cold phases, with outcomes depending on the relative timescales of cooling and mixing.

title: CANUCS/Technicolor Data Release 2: A Catalogue of Galaxy Structural Parameters in up to 29 HST+JWST bands and a Multi-Wavelength Exploration of the Galaxy Size-Mass Relation at $0.6 < z \leq 4$
comment: Submitted to ApJ; 30 pages, 16 figures; comments welcome. Data products available at https://niriss.github.io/data.html
summary: We present James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) results of a morphological study of galaxies in the CAnadian NIRISS Unbiased Cluster (CANUCS) and Technicolor surveys, observed in 19 medium- and broadband NIRCam filters in five CANUCS NIRCam Flanking Fields with rest-frame wavelength coverage between $\sim 0.2 - 3.2μm$. Using GALFIT, we measure the morphological parameters of $\sim$ 4,100 star-forming galaxies at $0.6 < z \leq 4$ with stellar masses of $8.5 < \text{log}(M_*/M_\odot) \leq 11.5$. This enables us to concurrently examine how galaxy size varies as a function of stellar mass, redshift, and rest-frame wavelength to provide a novel parametrization of the galaxy size-wavelength relation. Additionally, we analyze the evolution of the galaxy size-mass relation in the rest-frame optical and NIR with the introduction of wavelength as a free parameter. We report a gradient in the slope of the size-mass relation with respect to rest-frame wavelength with a critical crossover mass at $\sim 10^{9.5} M_\odot$. We propose this characteristic mass as the stellar mass at which galaxies transition between diffuse and compact morphologies. We concurrently present the data release of morphological measurements of the five CANUCS-Technicolor NIRCam Flanking Fields in which we provide structural parameters for $\sim$ 41,000 galaxies in up to 29 JWST+HST filters.

AI.tldr: This paper uses JWST NIRCam observations from the CANUCS and Technicolor surveys to measure morphological parameters of ~4,100 star-forming galaxies at 0.6 < z ≤ 4. It examines galaxy size as a function of stellar mass, redshift, and rest-frame wavelength, finding a critical crossover mass at ~10^9.5 M⊙ where galaxies transition between diffuse and compact morphologies. The study provides a data release of structural parameters for ~41,000 galaxies across 29 JWST+HST filters.
AI.motivation: To understand how galaxy size varies with stellar mass, redshift, and rest-frame wavelength, and to characterize the size-mass relation evolution in rest-frame optical and NIR, with particular interest in identifying a transition mass between diffuse and compact galaxy morphologies.
AI.method: JWST NIRCam observations from CANUCS and Technicolor surveys across 5 Flanking Fields using 19 medium- and broadband filters (rest-frame 0.2–3.2 μm). Morphological parameters measured using GALFIT on ~4,100 star-forming galaxies at 0.6 < z ≤ 4 with stellar masses 8.5 < log(M*/M⊙) ≤ 11.5. Size-mass relation analyzed with wavelength as a free parameter.
AI.result: A gradient in the slope of the size-mass relation with respect to rest-frame wavelength was found, with a critical crossover mass at ~10^9.5 M⊙, identified as the stellar mass marking the transition between diffuse and compact galaxy morphologies. A novel parametrization of the galaxy size-wavelength relation is provided.
AI.conclusion: The study presents a new data release of morphological measurements for ~41,000 galaxies across 29 JWST+HST filters in the five CANUCS-Technicolor NIRCam Flanking Fields, establishing a wavelength-dependent size-mass relation and identifying a characteristic transition mass separating diffuse and compact galaxies.

title: The host halo masses of AGNs and quasars at $z \sim 3-7$ with TNG-Cluster, FLAMINGO and other cosmological galaxy simulations
comment: Key Figures: 1,2, 5. Submitted to MNRAS (20 pages, 6 Figures)
summary: Most observations and clustering analyses suggest that quasars inhabit a narrow range of dark-matter halo masses ($10^{12-13}$ M$_{\odot}$) across cosmic time ($z\lesssim7$). Recent hydrodynamical simulations in gigaparsec-scale volumes now enable direct comparison of this picture with self-consistent galaxy-formation models. We quantify the relation between AGN bolometric luminosity and host halo mass before Cosmic Noon in TNG300, TNG-Cluster, FLAMINGO L1_m8 and L2p8_m9, and in smaller-volume simulations (Illustris, EAGLE, TNG100, and Simba). For AGNs with $L^{\mathrm{AGN}}_{\mathrm{bol}} \ge 10^{42}$ erg s$^{-1}$, more massive haloes host more luminous AGNs on average, but only up to a certain mass. The median luminosity-halo mass relation is highly non-linear, with large scatter, and flattens (FLAMINGO) or turns over (TNG300+TNG-Cluster) at halo mass, $M_{\mathrm{200,crit}} \gtrsim10^{12}$ M$_{\odot}$, at least at $z<5$-6. This high mass AGN quenching also manifests as a characteristic quasar host halo mass: in TNG300+TNG-Cluster, quasars ($L^{\mathrm{AGN}}_{\mathrm{bol}} \sim10^{45-47}$ erg s$^{-1}$) typically reside in haloes of mass $10^{12-12.5}$ M$_{\odot}$ at $z=3$-6, while FLAMINGO quasars extend to median masses of $\sim10^{12.8}$ M$_{\odot}$ at $z\sim3$-4. All simulations predict substantially larger scatter in AGN luminosity at fixed halo mass than in halo mass at fixed luminosity (up to 3 dex versus $\lesssim1$ dex between the 5th and 95th percentiles), implying weak coupling between halo growth and instantaneous SMBH accretion. Consequently, simulated quasar host masses broadly agree with observational estimates. The most luminous AGNs occupy increasingly rare haloes at earlier epochs but typically do not reside in the most massive haloes at any redshift up to $z\approx7$.

AI.tldr: Hydrodynamic simulations (TNG, FLAMINGO, etc.) show that AGN luminosity correlates non-linearly with halo mass, with quenching at high masses ($M_{200,\rm crit}\gtrsim10^{12}\,M_\odot$). Quasars typically inhabit haloes of $10^{12-12.5}\,M_\odot$ (TNG) or up to $\sim10^{12.8}\,M_\odot$ (FLAMINGO) at $z=3$–6, with large scatter implying weak coupling between halo growth and SMBH accretion.
AI.motivation: To test the prevailing observational picture that quasars occupy a narrow range of halo masses ($10^{12-13}\,M_\odot$) using self-consistent galaxy-formation models from large-volume hydrodynamic simulations.
AI.method: Analyzed AGN bolometric luminosity versus host halo mass in TNG300, TNG-Cluster, FLAMINGO (L1_m8, L2p8_m9), and smaller simulations (Illustris, EAGLE, TNG100, Simba) for AGNs with $L^{\rm AGN}_{\rm bol}\ge10^{42}$ erg s$^{-1}$, quantifying median relations, scatter, and redshift evolution.
AI.result: The $L_{\rm bol}$–$M_{\rm halo}$ relation is highly non-linear with large scatter: it flattens (FLAMINGO) or turns over (TNG) at $M_{200,\rm crit}\gtrsim10^{12}\,M_\odot$ at $z<5$–6. Quasars ($L_{\rm bol}\sim10^{45-47}$ erg s$^{-1}$) reside in haloes of $10^{12-12.5}\,M_\odot$ at $z=3$–6 (TNG) vs. $\sim10^{12.8}\,M_\odot$ at $z\sim3$–4 (FLAMINGO). Scatter in $L_{\rm bol}$ at fixed $M_{\rm halo}$ reaches $\sim3$ dex, while $M_{\rm halo}$ at fixed $L_{\rm bol}$ scatters $\lesssim1$ dex.
AI.conclusion: Halo growth and instantaneous SMBH accretion are weakly coupled; simulated quasar host masses broadly agree with observations. The most luminous AGNs reside in increasingly rare haloes at high $z$ but are not the most massive haloes at any redshift up to $z\approx7$.

title: The baryonic Tully-Fisher relation as an independent direct probe of cosmology and of the nature of dark matter
comment: 8 pages, 7 figures. Submitted to the journal
summary: The baryonic Tully-Fisher relation (BTFR), a well-established galaxy scaling relation linking the dynamical mass of rotation-supported galaxies through their maximum circular velocity to the baryonic luminous mass, has emerged over the decades as a fundamental scaling relation and as a robust calibrated distance indicator, thereby providing a robust benchmark to test galaxy formation and evolution theories as well as an independent probe of the expansion of the Universe. In this paper, we show for the first time that the BTFR is also simultaneously directly sensitive to the cosmological parameters $Ω_m$ and $σ_8$, the astrophysical feedback from supernovae (SNe) and active galactic nuclei (AGN), and the mass of warm dark matter particles $M_{\rm wdm}$, and can therefore be used as novel, direct probe of cosmology and fundamental physics. We perform simulation-based inference on the large DREAMS cosmological magneto-hydrodynamic simulations suite and train deep neural networks in the form of normalizing flows to estimate the posterior distributions of $Ω_m$, $σ_8$, $M_{\rm wdm}$ and the three astrophysical free parameters, given a BTFR measurement. Our framework is able to recover unbiased values for $Ω_m$ and $σ_8$, with subpercent deviations accuracy and a $\sim 2.6\%$ and $\sim 3.9\%$ median precision, respectively, to capture the warm dark matter particle mass $M_{\rm wdm}$ within a $\sim 30-35\%$ precision, as well as to constrain the SN feedback parameters (but not the one regulating AGN feedback). We conclude that, beyond its usage as a distance indicator and to constrain the baryon cycle and the feedback mechanisms shaping galaxy formation and evolution, the BTFR constitutes a direct independent probe of cosmology and fundamental physics and opens new promising avenues, to be explored with the future Square Kilometer Array.

AI.tldr: The paper shows for the first time that the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation (BTFR) is simultaneously sensitive to cosmological parameters (Ω_m, σ_8), warm dark matter particle mass (M_wdm), and astrophysical feedback from SNe and AGN. Using simulation-based inference on DREAMS simulations and normalizing flows, the authors demonstrate that BTFR can recover Ω_m and σ_8 with subpercent deviations and ~2.6-3.9% precision, constrain M_wdm within ~30-35% precision, and constrain SN feedback parameters, establishing BTFR as a direct independent probe of cosmology and fundamental physics.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate that the baryonic Tully-Fisher relation, traditionally used as a distance indicator and galaxy scaling relation, can serve as a direct probe of cosmological parameters (Ω_m, σ_8), warm dark matter particle mass, and astrophysical feedback mechanisms.
AI.method: Simulation-based inference on the DREAMS cosmological magneto-hydrodynamic simulations suite, using deep neural networks in the form of normalizing flows to estimate posterior distributions of Ω_m, σ_8, M_wdm, and three astrophysical free parameters from BTFR measurements.
AI.result: The framework recovers unbiased Ω_m and σ_8 with subpercent deviations and ~2.6% and ~3.9% median precision respectively, constrains M_wdm within ~30-35% precision, and constrains SN feedback parameters (but not AGN feedback).
AI.conclusion: Beyond its traditional use as a distance indicator and constraint on galaxy formation feedback, the BTFR constitutes a direct independent probe of cosmology and fundamental physics, with promising future avenues to be explored with the Square Kilometer Array.

title: Reconstructing the orbits of Milky Way dwarf galaxies: An LMC perspective
comment: 26 pages, 7 figures, 5 tables, 4 appendices. Submitted to A&A
summary: The orbital histories of the dwarf satellites of the Milky Way (MW) are key to understanding their evolution and placing their present-day properties in a dynamical context. We present the results of the orbit integration of 72 dwarfs in the vicinity of the MW, based on accurate 6D phase-space coordinates from the literature and a suite of six realistic, time-evolving gravitational potentials that account for the mutual interaction of the MW and the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC). We provide the largest catalogue of orbital parameters for MW dwarfs to date, in terms of both galaxy sample size and range of potentials explored. We also assess the binding status of the dwarfs and estimate their infall times, finding that the majority of them have spent the last 5 Gyr within the MW virial radius. From the reconstructed orbits, we identify ten likely LMC satellites, several of which have experienced very close passages within the LMC stellar disc. For the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC), we find that its most recent pericentre about the LMC ($\sim$8 kpc, $\sim$170 Myr ago) is consistent with predictions from the direct collision scenario proposed to explain the LMC's offset and tilted bar. We also note a broad temporal coincidence between previous SMC pericentres and star formation rate peaks reported in both Magellanic Clouds, suggesting a causal connection. Finally, we identify Grus II and Tucana IV as possible MW satellites recently captured by the LMC, based on their pronounced orbital deflections and velocities relative to the LMC.

AI.tldr: This paper reconstructs orbits for 72 Milky Way dwarf satellites using 6D phase-space data and six time-varying gravitational potentials that include MW-LMC interactions. It provides the largest orbital catalogue for MW dwarfs, identifies ten likely LMC satellites, finds SMC pericenters coinciding with star formation peaks, and identifies Grus II and Tucana IV as possible recently captured MW satellites by the LMC.
AI.motivation: Understanding the orbital histories of Milky Way dwarf satellites is essential for interpreting their present-day properties in a dynamical context, yet previous studies lacked large samples and realistic, time-evolving potentials that account for MW-LMC mutual interactions.
AI.method: Orbit integration of 72 MW dwarfs using accurate 6D phase-space coordinates from the literature and six realistic, time-evolving gravitational potentials incorporating MW-LMC interactions.
AI.result: Largest catalogue of orbital parameters for MW dwarfs; majority spent last 5 Gyr within MW virial radius; identified ten likely LMC satellites; SMC's recent pericentre (~8 kpc, ~170 Myr ago) consistent with direct collision scenario; temporal coincidence between SMC pericenters and star formation rate peaks; identified Grus II and Tucana IV as possible recently captured MW satellites by the LMC.
AI.conclusion: The reconstructed orbits reveal dynamical connections between the Magellanic Clouds and their surrounding dwarfs, support the direct collision scenario for the LMC's bar, and suggest a causal link between SMC pericenters and star formation bursts, while highlighting ongoing satellite capture processes in the MW-LMC system.

title: Controlling instrumental systematics for the BICEP inflation survey
comment: Conference proceedings - Rencontres de Moriond, Cosmology, 2026
summary: The BICEP series of experiments has been observing CMB polarisation from the South Pole for over 20 years, with the goal of constraining inflationary gravitational waves. The upcoming data release, using data taken through 2024, is forecasted to constrain the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$ at the level of $σ(r) \sim 0.005$ (including delensing), with the longer-term goal of reaching $σ(r) \sim 0.001$ by 2034. As the survey sensitivity increases, it is crucial to control instrumental systematics to unprecedented levels, and our goal is to limit dominant sources of systematics to 20% of $σ(r)$ or lower. Achieving this requires careful instrumental characterisation and dedicated end-to-end studies to evaluate the impact of each systematic on cosmological parameters. We first present the BICEP calibration program, which characterises the optical, spectral, and polarisation response of the receivers. We then describe the analysis strategies implemented to identify and mitigate systematic contamination, and we detail simulations used to evaluate the impact of residual effects. We focus in particular on beam systematics, the dominant source of systematics for BICEP receivers. Finally, we report preliminary estimates of the expected level of systematic contamination for upcoming BICEP results, and we discuss approaches to evaluate and mitigate instrumental systematics for future surveys.

AI.tldr: BICEP experiments have been measuring CMB polarisation for over 20 years to constrain inflationary gravitational waves. Upcoming data (through 2024) will constrain tensor-to-scalar ratio r to σ(r)~0.005, aiming for σ(r)~0.001 by 2034. This paper describes the calibration program, systematics control strategies, simulations, and mitigation approaches, focusing on beam systematics as the dominant systematic source.
AI.motivation: To constrain inflationary gravitational waves via CMB polarisation measurements, with the goal of reaching increasingly sensitive tensor-to-scalar ratio constraints (σ(r)~0.005 now, σ(r)~0.001 by 2034).
AI.method: Calibration program characterising optical, spectral, and polarisation responses of receivers; analysis strategies to identify and mitigate systematic contamination; end-to-end simulations to evaluate residual effects on cosmological parameters.
AI.result: Forecasted constraint on tensor-to-scalar ratio at σ(r)~0.005 with delensing for data through 2024; preliminary estimates of expected systematic contamination levels for upcoming results.
AI.conclusion: Dominant systematics (especially beam systematics) must be limited to ≤20% of σ(r); detailed instrumental characterisation and simulation-based evaluation are essential; approaches discussed extend to future surveys.

title: A novel data-driven approach to extract stellar population properties from galaxy spectra using absorption indices
comment: 20 pages, including 10 figures and 1 table. Submitted to MNRAS
summary: In an era of highly complex machine learning methods that often are informative but not straightforward to interpret, Principal Component Analysis (PCA) offers a simple, easily interpretable approach. With no fitting parameters, it extracts the most salient statistical trends in data without the need for training sets. In this paper, we explore a large range of composite stellar population models defined for detailed analyses of galaxy spectra from surveys. Six of the most prominent spectral indices are targeted to visualize a PCA-based latent space created by the model data. The age-metallicity degeneracy is broken in the 3-dimensional space spanned by the first three eigenvectors, but we emphasize that non-trivial combinations of all six absorption indices are needed for this. Moreover, the last eigenvector suggests an intriguing tug of war between two Balmer indices: H$γ_A$ and $Hδ_A$, that can help discern the presence of recent bursting behaviour, as it exploits the different behaviour of the two indices over timescales $\sim$0.5-1 Gyr. Comparisons can be made between SDSS and LEGA-C galaxy spectra based on the latent space created by the models. This method, based on pure data, produces excellent results in agreement with standard SPS model fitting techniques, allowing for the study of stellar populations in a variety of surveys or observational/synthetic databases on solid ground.

AI.tldr: PCA applied to six spectral indices from composite stellar population models creates a latent space where the age-metallicity degeneracy is broken, and the last eigenvector reveals a Balmer index tug-of-war (Hγ_A vs Hδ_A) that can detect recent bursting behavior over ~0.5-1 Gyr timescales, enabling stellar population comparisons across surveys like SDSS and LEGA-C.
AI.motivation: Complex machine learning methods are often uninterpretable, so the authors seek a simple, interpretable approach (PCA) to analyze galaxy spectra without fitting parameters or training sets.
AI.method: PCA is applied to a large set of composite stellar population models using six prominent spectral indices; the latent space (first three eigenvectors) is visualized and analyzed for physical interpretability.
AI.result: The age-metallicity degeneracy is broken in 3D eigenvector space; the last eigenvector reveals a competition between Hγ_A and Hδ_A that traces bursting behavior on ~0.5-1 Gyr timescales. Results agree with standard SPS fitting.
AI.conclusion: Pure data-driven PCA produces results consistent with standard SPS model fitting, providing a solid basis for studying stellar populations across diverse surveys and databases.

title: Constraints on Stable Scalar-Tensor Dark Energy from DESI Data and Solar System Tests
summary: We investigate the viability of scalar-tensor (quintessence) models of dark energy with a quartic polynomial nonminimal coupling to gravity and a linear scalar potential. The polynomial nonminimal coupling is used to ensure that the field is well stabilized in the early universe. We perform a systematic exploration of the parameter space spanned by the quadratic and quartic nonminimal couplings, as well as the slope of the potential. We confront the predictions of the model with the latest Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) constraints on the dark energy equation of state and also with complementary bounds from local tests of gravity, including solar system constraints and limits on the time variation of the effective Newton's constant. We identify bands in parameter space where all these constraints are satisfied, finding such bands to be very narrow.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates scalar-tensor quintessence models with quartic polynomial nonminimal coupling and linear potential, finding very narrow viable parameter bands that satisfy DESI constraints, local gravity tests, and limits on Newton's constant variation.
AI.motivation: To assess the viability of scalar-tensor (quintessence) dark energy models with a quartic polynomial nonminimal coupling and linear scalar potential, in light of the latest DESI data and gravitational constraints.
AI.method: Systematic exploration of parameter space (quadratic and quartic nonminimal couplings, potential slope); confrontation with DESI constraints on dark energy equation of state, solar system tests, and time variation of effective Newton's constant.
AI.result: Very narrow bands in parameter space satisfy all constraints simultaneously.
AI.conclusion: Scalar-tensor quintessence models with quartic polynomial nonminimal coupling and linear potential are highly constrained, with only narrow viable parameter regions.

title: GA-NIFS: The interplay between feedback and star formation at 3 < z < 9 probed by JWST/NIRSpec IFU
summary: The study of starburst- and AGN-driven feedback is fundamental for understanding the processes that shape galaxy growth, quench star formation, and drive the co-evolution of galaxies and their central black holes. We present a spatially resolved study of six galaxies at $3 < z < 9$, including starburst- and AGN-dominated systems, observed with JWST/NIRSpec IFU in low- ($R \sim 100$) and high-resolution ($R \sim 2700$) mode. Previous analysis of $R \sim 2700$ data revealed ionized outflows in all these galaxies. We explore possible links between outflows and stellar population properties to assess the mechanisms driving galaxy evolution at early epochs. Combining the spatially resolved stellar population analysis with the outflow properties, we find that the most massive galaxies ($M_\star > 5 \times 10^{10} M_\odot$) with strong AGN-driven ionized outflows show evidence of past quenching episodes occurring within the last $\sim 100$--$300$ Myr, mainly in the nuclear regions ($r < 3$ kpc). In contrast, higher-redshift ($z > 5$) and less massive ($M_\star < 10^{10} M_\odot$) starburst galaxies with powerful (starburst-driven) outflows appear to have experienced continuous growth, with no clear sign of quenching. Massive galaxies with weaker outflows do not show evidence of quenching in their history. One massive AGN host (GS20936) shows evidence for a recent ($10$--$30$ Myr) rejuvenation phase, likely fueled by a recent major merger. These results suggest that (AGN-driven) outflows can already play a key role in shaping the SFHs of massive galaxies at early cosmic epochs.

AI.tldr: JWST/NIRSpec IFU observations of six galaxies at 3<z<9 reveal that massive galaxies with strong AGN-driven outflows show quenching in the last 100-300 Myr, while lower-mass starburst galaxies with powerful outflows exhibit continuous growth, suggesting AGN-driven outflows shape early massive galaxy evolution.
AI.motivation: To understand how starburst- and AGN-driven feedback influences galaxy growth, star formation quenching, and the co-evolution of galaxies and their central black holes at early cosmic epochs.
AI.method: Spatially resolved study of six galaxies at 3<z<9 using JWST/NIRSpec IFU in low- (R~100) and high-resolution (R~2700) mode, combining outflow property analysis with stellar population analysis.
AI.result: Massive galaxies (M⋆>5×10¹⁰ M☉) with strong AGN-driven outflows show past quenching within ~100-300 Myr in nuclear regions (r<3 kpc); higher-redshift (z>5) less massive starburst galaxies show continuous growth; one AGN host shows rejuvenation from a recent merger.
AI.conclusion: AGN-driven outflows can play a key role in shaping the star formation histories of massive galaxies at early cosmic epochs.

title: Optimal marked statistics from the Effective Field Theory of Large Scale Structure
summary: We present a simple and robust framework to assess the information content of the power spectrum of a marked density field within the Effective Field Theory of Large Scale Structure, providing a physically motivated regime of validity of perturbation theory for such fields. We optimize the choice of mark to maximize the constraining power on cosmological parameters, focusing on the resulting reduction of parameter uncertainties. After marginalizing over the small-scale counterterms, we find improvements in the parameter error bars by a factor of approximately $1.30$-$2.3$, $1.3$-$8.3$, and $1.2$-$2.5$ for $Ω_m$, $σ_8$, and $h$, respectively, depending on redshift and smoothing scale. The optimized mark exhibits a simple functional form, for which we provide a physical interpretation in terms of its response to the underlying density field. These results demonstrate the potential of marked statistics as a tool to extract additional cosmological information beyond standard two-point analyses and open a pathway for further exploration of nonlinear transformations of the density field.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a framework within the Effective Field Theory of Large Scale Structure to assess and optimize marked power spectra for extracting cosmological information, showing significant improvements in parameter constraints (Ωₘ, σ₈, h) beyond standard two-point analyses.
AI.motivation: To develop a physically motivated, robust framework for assessing the information content of marked power spectra and to optimize the choice of mark for maximizing constraining power on cosmological parameters, moving beyond standard two-point statistics.
AI.method: Using the Effective Field Theory of Large Scale Structure to define a regime of validity for perturbation theory of marked density fields; optimizing the mark functional form to minimize parameter uncertainties; marginalizing over small-scale counterterms.
AI.result: Improvements in parameter error bars by factors of ~1.30–2.3 (Ωₘ), 1.3–8.3 (σ₈), and 1.2–2.5 (h), depending on redshift and smoothing scale. The optimized mark has a simple functional form with a clear physical interpretation in terms of its response to the density field.
AI.conclusion: Marked statistics are a promising tool for extracting additional cosmological information beyond standard two-point analyses, opening pathways for further exploration of nonlinear transformations of the density field.

title: The S-PLUS Fornax Project (S+FP): Fornax-like clusters in cosmological hydrodynamical simulations
comment: 15 pages, 6 figures. Accepted for publication in A&A
summary: The Fornax galaxy cluster constitutes a suitable laboratory to explore the evolution of galaxies in a dense environment. Recently, the Southern Photometric Local Universe Survey (S-PLUS) has obtained unprecedented photometric information of Fornax, revealing new features regarding its galaxy populations and surrounding regions. In this context, simulations are invaluable tools to interpret the past, present and fate of such observational findings. We aim to deliver a robust photometric catalog of simulated Fornax-like systems in cosmological context, to consistently contrast them with S-PLUS data. We analyze Fornax analogs from the EAGLE and IllustrisTNG simulations, selected using observed properties of the Fornax cluster and its central galaxy NGC 1399. For each system, we generated synthetic photometry in the 12 S-PLUS bands using the SKIRT radiative transfer code, reproducing the instrumental configuration of the S-PLUS survey. Simulated data cubes, mock images, spectral energy distributions, magnitudes and colors were obtained for each galaxy in our selected simulated Fornax analogs. The synthetic photometry and spectra derived from simulations show a good agreement with the S-PLUS observations. We identify particular systems which show some similarity with the spatial distribution of galaxies in Fornax. Such simulated candidates reproduce the observed color-magnitude relation and the spatial substructure between the cluster core and the Fornax A region. Also, simulated galaxies are bluer at higher cluster-centric distances, in agreement with observations. Although modest discrepancies were obtained between the observed and simulated color-magnitude diagrams in some cases, our results support the suitability of our selection criteria and synthetic photometry, and the reliability of current cosmological simulations to reproduce key general features of the Fornax cluster.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a robust photometric catalog of simulated Fornax-like galaxy clusters from EAGLE and IllustrisTNG simulations, generating synthetic S-PLUS photometry via SKIRT radiative transfer. The simulated data show good agreement with observed S-PLUS color-magnitude relations, spatial substructure, and cluster-centric color gradients, supporting the reliability of cosmological simulations to reproduce key features of the Fornax cluster.
AI.motivation: The Fornax galaxy cluster is an ideal laboratory for studying galaxy evolution in dense environments. Recent S-PLUS photometric data have revealed new features, and simulations are needed to interpret these observational findings and understand the past, present, and future of the cluster.
AI.method: Fornax analogs were selected from EAGLE and IllustrisTNG simulations based on observed properties of the Fornax cluster and NGC 1399. Synthetic photometry in 12 S-PLUS bands was generated using the SKIRT radiative transfer code, reproducing the S-PLUS instrumental configuration. Data cubes, mock images, SEDs, magnitudes, and colors were produced for each galaxy.
AI.result: Synthetic photometry and spectra show good agreement with S-PLUS observations. Specific simulated systems reproduce the observed color-magnitude relation, spatial substructure between the core and Fornax A region, and the trend of bluer galaxies at larger cluster-centric distances. Some modest discrepancies in color-magnitude diagrams were noted.
AI.conclusion: The selection criteria and synthetic photometry are suitable, and current cosmological simulations reliably reproduce key general features of the Fornax cluster, supporting their use for interpreting observational data.

title: Impact of non-Gaussian likelihood on cosmological constraints from the thermal Sunyaev--Zel'dovich power spectrum: a simulation-based inference analysis
comment: 22 pages, 15 figures, submitted to Physical Review D
summary: The thermal Sunyaev--Zel'dovich (tSZ) power spectrum is a sensitive probe of cosmology and cluster astrophysics, but its statistics are non-Gaussian because the signal receives a significant contribution from rare, massive, low-redshift galaxy clusters. As a result, a Gaussian likelihood fails to describe the statistics of its power spectrum on large scales. We use simulation-based inference (SBI) to test the accuracy of the standard Gaussian power-spectrum likelihood for a \textit{Planck}-like tSZ analysis. Using halo-based simulations of full-sky Compton-$y$ maps, we train neural posterior and likelihood estimators and compare the resulting constraints with those from a Gaussian likelihood assumption. Using only multipoles $\ell < 1000$, we find that the Gaussian likelihood assumption gives unbiased cosmological constraints, while the SBI-based inference shows a mild broadening of the posterior distributions for the amplitudes of residual foregrounds. This suggests that the Gaussian likelihood assumption is sufficiently accurate for cosmological inference for a \textit{Planck}-like tSZ analysis, while SBI provides a useful validation tool to model non-Gaussian likelihoods beyond analytic approximations.

AI.tldr: This paper tests the accuracy of the standard Gaussian likelihood assumption for the thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (tSZ) power spectrum using simulation-based inference (SBI). For a Planck-like analysis with multipoles ℓ<1000, the Gaussian likelihood yields unbiased cosmological constraints, though SBI reveals mild broadening of posterior distributions for residual foreground amplitudes.
AI.motivation: The tSZ power spectrum is a sensitive cosmological probe, but its statistics are inherently non-Gaussian due to contributions from rare, massive, low-redshift clusters, making the standard Gaussian likelihood potentially inaccurate on large scales.
AI.method: Simulation-based inference (SBI) with neural posterior and likelihood estimators applied to halo-based simulations of full-sky Compton-y maps, compared against a standard Gaussian power-spectrum likelihood for a Planck-like tSZ analysis using multipoles ℓ<1000.
AI.result: The Gaussian likelihood assumption gives unbiased cosmological constraints, while SBI shows a mild broadening of posterior distributions for residual foreground amplitudes.
AI.conclusion: The Gaussian likelihood assumption is sufficiently accurate for cosmological inference in Planck-like tSZ analyses, while SBI serves as a useful validation tool for modeling non-Gaussian likelihoods beyond analytic approximations.

title: Identifying Warped Galaxies in Pan-STARRS and Euclid using Deep Convolutional Neural Network
summary: Warped galactic discs are common, yet their detection remains challenging, as the outskirts of galaxies are typically faint. Advances in deep imaging surveys improve the detectability of such features, while machine learning enables efficient analysis of large datasets. Using the Pan-STARRS EGIPS catalogue, we develop a deep learning framework by fine-tuning the Zoobot convNext-nano model on 1000 edge-on galaxy FITS images to distinguish warped and non-warped edge-on galaxies with 83\% accuracy. The trained model is then applied to a larger sample, identifying 2088 warped and 1398 non-warped galaxies with a high prediction probability threshold ($\geq 0.85$). Additionally, we use the model to predict on 3226 edge-on galaxies from the Euclid Q1 survey, demonstrating the model's ability to generalise across datasets with differing resolutions. To analyse the model predictions, we employ LayerCAM to identify the regions of galaxy images that contribute to the classification. We find that warped galaxies differ primarily in their structural properties, exhibiting lower axis ratios and higher asymmetry. Warped galaxies were found to be bluer, with younger stellar populations and enhanced star formation. These results highlight the effectiveness of deep learning methods in identifying subtle morphological features, such as warps, and demonstrate their potential for studying structural properties of galaxies in current and upcoming large imaging surveys.

AI.tldr: This paper uses a fine-tuned Zoobot convNext-nano deep learning model on Pan-STARRS EGIPS edge-on galaxy images to detect warped galactic discs with 83% accuracy. The model identifies 2088 warped and 1398 non-warped galaxies and generalizes to Euclid Q1 data. Warped galaxies show lower axis ratios, higher asymmetry, bluer colors, younger stellar populations, and enhanced star formation.
AI.motivation: Warped galactic discs are common but difficult to detect because galaxy outskirts are faint. The authors aim to leverage deep imaging surveys and deep learning to efficiently detect and study these subtle morphological features in large datasets.
AI.method: Fine-tuned the Zoobot convNext-nano model on 1000 edge-on galaxy FITS images from the Pan-STARRS EGIPS catalogue to classify warped vs. non-warped galaxies. Applied the trained model to a larger sample and to Euclid Q1 data. Used LayerCAM for interpretability and analyzed structural and photometric properties.
AI.result: Achieved 83% classification accuracy. Identified 2088 warped and 1398 non-warped galaxies at high confidence (≥0.85). Model generalized to Euclid Q1 data. Warped galaxies exhibit lower axis ratios, higher asymmetry, bluer colors, younger stellar populations, and enhanced star formation.
AI.conclusion: Deep learning is effective for detecting subtle morphological features like warps and shows potential for studying galaxy structural properties in current and upcoming large imaging surveys.

title: Impact of 21-cm foreground mitigation strategies on reionization power spectrum constraints
summary: The 21-cm signal probes the intergalactic medium during the Epoch of Reionization (EoR) but is overwhelmed by astrophysical foregrounds orders of magnitude stronger than the cosmological signal. We evaluate two mitigation strategies: (i) Foreground Avoidance, restricting analysis to the EoR window in Fourier space, and (ii) Foreground Removal via Gaussian Process Regression, which exploits spectral smoothness to statistically separate contaminants and reclaim modes within the contaminated wedge. Both introduce systematic biases of up to $\approx$1$σ$ in astrophysical parameters such as the minimum star-forming halo mass and ionising escape fraction, with avoidance posteriors consistently broader than removal owing to its restricted visibility coverage. The global reionization history is recovered within the 95% credible interval, though the neutral fraction at late reionization epochs shows a persistent bias reflecting the difficulty of its inference from the power spectrum alone. Multi-redshift inference is susceptible to contamination from poorly mitigated bins. Excluding such bins significantly reduces parameter biases, but identifying them requires independent quality metrics. When restricted to identical length scales, both strategies recover similar power spectra, yielding posteriors in similar regions.

AI.tldr: The paper compares Foreground Avoidance vs. Gaussian Process Regression-based Foreground Removal for 21-cm signal analysis during the Epoch of Reionization, finding both introduce ~1σ biases in astrophysical parameters, with avoidance yielding broader posteriors; reionization history is recovered within 95% CI but late-epoch neutral fraction remains biased.
AI.motivation: The 21-cm signal from the EoR is overwhelmed by strong astrophysical foregrounds, necessitating effective mitigation strategies to extract cosmological information.
AI.method: Two foreground mitigation strategies are evaluated: (i) Foreground Avoidance (restricting analysis to the EoR window in Fourier space) and (ii) Foreground Removal using Gaussian Process Regression to exploit spectral smoothness for statistical separation of contaminants.
AI.result: Both strategies introduce systematic biases up to ~1σ in astrophysical parameters; avoidance yields broader posteriors due to restricted visibility coverage. Global reionization history is within 95% CI, but late-epoch neutral fraction shows persistent bias. Multi-redshift inference suffers from poorly mitigated bins; excluding such bins reduces biases but requires independent quality metrics. When restricted to identical length scales, both strategies recover similar power spectra and posteriors.
AI.conclusion: Neither strategy is unbiased; foreground removal recovers tighter constraints but both require careful quality control, especially for multi-redshift inference and late-epoch neutral fraction estimation.

title: Uncovering DM distribution by combining stellar kinematics and integrated HI spectra: method validation
comment: 23 pages, 18 figures; submitted to Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: We determine the dark matter (DM) distribution in galaxies by jointly modelling stellar kinematics from IFU observations and the gaseous kinematics encoded in a single integrated HI spectrum. The stellar kinematics are described by a triaxial orbit-superposition Schwarzschild model, while the HI gas is described by an idealised disc model; both are governed by the same gravitational potential. The potential comprises the stellar mass, a generalised NFW DM halo, and a central black hole. We validate the method on 58 simulated galaxies generated from the TNG50 cosmological simulation. For each galaxy, we create two versions of mock data with azimuthal angles viewed side-on and end-on thus 116 mock observations in total. Our model recovers the total mass, stellar mass, and DM mass profiles within the data range; the median DM mass of the 58 simulated galaxies is recovered with a relative systematic bias smaller than 20% across all radii from 2--20 kpc. The statistical uncertainties on the DM masses within 5 kpc remain similar to those found with the model constrained by IFU data only. In contrast, the relative uncertainty on the DM mass in the outer regions decreases once the HI spectrum is included; at 20 kpc, it drops markedly, from about 85% to roughly 30%. The DM density slope defined explicitly in the gNFW model is systematically underestimated and thus does not yield a reliable quantity from observations using our approach. Instead, we introduce density slopes evaluated between 2 and 20 kpc, which are statistically well recovered for both the total mass and the DM mass. We demonstrate the reliability of this method in uncovering DM distribution and emphasize its promise for application to large samples of observed galaxies.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a method to determine dark matter distribution in galaxies by jointly modeling stellar kinematics (from IFU observations) and gaseous kinematics (from a single integrated HI spectrum) within a common gravitational potential. Validated on 58 simulated TNG50 galaxies (116 mock observations), the model recovers mass profiles well, with DM mass bias <20% across 2–20 kpc. Including HI data reduces outer-region DM mass uncertainty from ~85% to ~30% at 20 kpc. The gNFW slope is systematically biased, but density slopes between 2–20 kpc are reliably recovered.
AI.motivation: To reliably determine the dark matter distribution in galaxies by combining stellar and gaseous kinematic tracers, overcoming limitations of using only stellar kinematics (large outer-region uncertainties) and enabling application to large observed galaxy samples.
AI.method: Jointly model stellar kinematics (from IFU observations via triaxial orbit-superposition Schwarzschild model) and gaseous kinematics (from a single integrated HI spectrum via an idealized disc model), governed by the same gravitational potential (stellar mass + generalized NFW DM halo + central black hole). Validated on 58 simulated TNG50 galaxies with 116 mock observations (side-on and end-on projections).
AI.result: Total mass, stellar mass, and DM mass profiles are recovered well within the data range. Median DM mass bias <20% across 2–20 kpc. Statistical uncertainties of DM mass within 5 kpc similar to IFU-only models. Outer-region (20 kpc) DM mass uncertainty drops from ~85% to ~30% with HI data included. gNFW DM density slope systematically underestimated; density slopes between 2–20 kpc are reliably recovered.
AI.conclusion: The joint modeling approach reliably recovers DM distribution, significantly improves outer-region DM constraints via HI data, and is promising for application to large observed galaxy samples.

title: Lensed hot stars with HST in the 2030s
comment: 6 pages, 3 figures; white paper submitted in response to the Space Telescope Science Institute call: Building a Roadmap for Hubble science into the 2030s
summary: In the late 20th century, the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) revolutionized astronomy, showing the Universe with a detail never seen before in the ultraviolet (UV), optical and infrared (IR) bands. In the early 2020s, the James Webb Space Telescope started a similar revolution in the IR. The launch of Roman in late 2026 challenges the reign of HST in the optical band, but even after Roman's launch, HST will remain as the only telescope capable of high-quality imaging in the UV band. In the optical bands, HST provides superior resolution than Roman for point sources. Although equipped with more sensitive MOS, Roman's sensors have a pixel size about 3 times larger than HST's CCDs, hence undersampling the point-spread-function, and resulting in a worse spatial resolution. The UV-capable and higher-resolution of HST in the UV and optical band, makes HST the best instrument for specific science cases. This paper responds to the "Building a Roadmap for Hubble science into the 2030s" call and focuses on science with lensed hot stars at $z>0.5$ in the UV and optical bands, exploiting the features that makes HST the best instrument in the UV/optical until the launch of the Habitable World Observatory in the 2040s.

AI.tldr: This paper argues that despite the upcoming Roman Space Telescope, HST remains essential for UV and high-resolution optical astronomy, particularly for studying lensed hot stars at z>0.5, until the Habitable World Observatory launches in the 2040s.
AI.motivation: To respond to the "Building a Roadmap for Hubble science into the 2030s" call and justify HST's continued scientific value in the UV/optical bands after Roman's launch, specifically for science cases requiring UV capability and high spatial resolution.
AI.method: The paper compares HST, Roman, and JWST capabilities across UV, optical, and IR bands; identifies HST's unique advantages (UV imaging, superior point-source resolution in optical); and proposes a focused science case on lensed hot stars at z>0.5 as a demonstrator.
AI.result: HST remains the only telescope capable of high-quality UV imaging after Roman's launch, and provides superior optical resolution for point sources compared to Roman (which undersamples the PSF due to 3× larger pixels).
AI.conclusion: HST is uniquely positioned to serve specific science cases in UV and high-resolution optical astronomy into the 2030s, until the Habitable World Observatory becomes operational in the 2040s.

title: GATOS N: Extended circumnuclear dust emission in nearby Seyfert galaxies surveyed by JWST/MIRI
summary: The subarcsecond angular resolution and stable background of JWST has given us the first high-fidelity images of the arcsecond-scale environment around Active Galactic Nuclei (AGNs) in the nearby Universe. With mid-infrared (MIR) surface brightness sensitivities that are much deeper than the best ground-based instruments, the Mid-InfraRed Instrument imager (MIRIM) now allows us to understand the structure and thermal properties of dust using information over wavelengths of $5$-$25$ $μ$m, almost all of the MIR range. We present a Cycle 1 JWST MIRIM survey of Seyfert galaxies with the express aim of characterising AGN-heated dust in the central few 100 pcs, and searching for signatures of dust-laden nuclear outflows. This paper outlines the motivation behind the programme, the data reduction and analysis techniques used to isolate the nuclear and extended emission, and a comparison of the observed MIR structures with those seen in other phases (stars, ionised and molecular gas, absorbing dust). In concert with earlier studies that used these data, we conclude that resolved AGN-heated dust is widespread in the Seyfert population, extending out to a few hundred pcs from the nucleus and often displaying a higher surface-brightness compared to the more widespread star-forming dusty circumnuclear disk. Even after accounting for contamination from emission lines in the MIRI filters, we find strong spatial correlations between MIR dust emission and the AGN-ionised gas in the narrow-line region (NLR).

AI.tldr: JWST MIRIM survey of Seyfert galaxies resolves AGN-heated dust on scales of a few hundred parsecs, showing strong spatial correlations with NLR ionized gas and higher surface brightness compared to star-forming dusty disks.
AI.motivation: To characterize AGN-heated dust in the central few hundred parsecs of Seyfert galaxies and search for signatures of dust-laden nuclear outflows, leveraging JWST's superior angular resolution and MIR sensitivity.
AI.method: Cycle 1 JWST MIRIM survey of Seyfert galaxies using MIR imaging (5-25 μm), with data reduction and analysis techniques to isolate nuclear and extended emission, and cross-comparison with observations of stars, ionized/molecular gas, and absorbing dust.
AI.result: Resolved AGN-heated dust is widespread in Seyfert galaxies, extending to a few hundred parsecs from the nucleus, with higher surface brightness than star-forming circumnuclear disks. Strong spatial correlations exist between MIR dust emission and AGN-ionized gas in the NLR, even after accounting for emission-line contamination in MIRI filters.
AI.conclusion: JWST MIRIM enables detailed characterization of AGN-heated dust structures in nearby Seyferts, revealing widespread dust emission correlated with NLR ionized gas, supporting the connection between AGN activity and dust distribution in galactic nuclei.

title: A new CIGALE module for modeling AGN emission lines
summary:
Aims. The increasing discovery of high-redshift AGNs in recent years imposes more stringent requirements on spectral analysis tools for deriving the properties of AGNs and their host galaxies from emission-line diagnostics. To address this need, we develop a new module for the popular SED-fitting tool Code Investigating GALaxy Emission (CIGALE), the [nebular_AGN] module, which enables the efficient and flexible simulation and fitting of emission lines originating from the broad-line regions (BLRs) and narrow-line regions (NLRs) of AGNs, and allows the estimation of the physical properties of these regions.
  Methods. We use the spectral synthesis code Cloudy to construct the database for the new module. Based on the X-ray and accretion disk continua implemented in CIGALE, we generate the incident radiation fields of the models. We then adopt the AGN geometry and dust settings implemented in CIGALE to define a flexible set of physical parameters for the gas clouds, thereby producing a comprehensive database for the [nebular_AGN] module.
  Results. We benchmark the [nebular_AGN] module using a quasar composite spectrum, an empirical metallicity calibration, and observational data from X-ray-selected AGNs. Our module can approximately reproduce the majority of quasar emission-line profiles, cover the key emission-line ratios observed in AGN samples, and provide an assessment of their physical properties. For specific combinations of parameters, the metallicity derived by our module is consistent with the empirical formula. We further compare our models with other photoionization models used to simulate AGN NLR emission, and perform a line-sensitivity study to identify the most effective diagnostic lines for each parameter in our module. Finally, we confirm that the dust attenuation law plays an important role in SED fitting.

AI.tldr: The paper presents the [nebular_AGN] module for CIGALE, a flexible SED-fitting tool that simulates and fits emission lines from AGN BLRs and NLRs using Cloudy-generated models, benchmarking it against quasar composites, metallicity calibrations, and observed AGN data.
AI.motivation: The increasing discovery of high-redshift AGNs demands more robust spectral analysis tools for deriving AGN and host galaxy properties from emission-line diagnostics.
AI.method: The module uses Cloudy to construct a photoionization database based on AGN continua, geometry, and dust settings already implemented in CIGALE, enabling flexible parameterization of gas cloud properties for BLR and NLR emission-line simulation and fitting.
AI.result: The module reproduces quasar emission-line profiles, covers key AGN emission-line ratios, yields metallicities consistent with empirical calibrations, and identifies the most effective diagnostic lines for each parameter; dust attenuation law is confirmed to be important in SED fitting.
AI.conclusion: The [nebular_AGN] module provides an efficient and flexible tool for modeling and fitting AGN emission lines within CIGALE, enabling estimation of physical properties of BLRs and NLRs across a wide range of AGN populations.

title: From THESAN-ZOOM to JWST: Predicting ionizing photon escape and the rise of UV-bright reionization sources
summary: Understanding the sources and evolution of cosmic reionization remains a central challenge in astrophysics, with the escape of ionizing Lyman-continuum (LyC) photons from early galaxies representing a major uncertainty. In this work, we use more than 35,000 galaxy realisations from the THESAN-ZOOM cosmological radiation-hydrodynamic simulations to identify indirect diagnostics of the LyC photon escape fraction ($f_\mathrm{esc}$) and the LyC photon escape rate ($\dot{N}_\mathrm{ion,esc}$) across the redshift range $z=3-16$. We train random forest regression models using these diagnostics to predict both quantities. We present four models: two trained with the full set of simulation-derived indicators to predict $f_\mathrm{esc}$ and $\dot{N}_\mathrm{ion,esc}$, and two restricted to observables accessible to JWST photometric surveys. We find the 10-to-100$\,$Myr star-formation rate ratio ($\mathrm{SFR}_{10} / \mathrm{SFR}_{100}$) and the gas-to-stellar mass ratio ($M_\mathrm{gas} / M_*$) to be the strongest diagnostics of $f_\mathrm{esc}$, suggesting a strong relationship between ionizing photon escape and gas clearing through bursty star formation. In contrast, rest-frame UV ($1500 \, Å$) absolute magnitude ($M_\mathrm{UV}$) dominates $\dot{N}_\mathrm{ion,esc}$ prediction. Motivated by the strong predictive power of $M_\mathrm{UV}$, we combine observed UV luminosity functions with derived $\dot{N}_\mathrm{ion,esc} - M_\mathrm{UV}$ relations to construct histories of reionization. These are consistent with observational constraints, avoiding the recently reported crisis in the ionizing photon budget. Our analysis suggests that the bulk of reionization occurred rapidly after $z \approx 8$, driven by UV-bright galaxies, with the $M_\mathrm{UV} < -17$ populations providing the dominant contribution.

AI.tldr: Using >35,000 galaxy simulations from THESAN-ZOOM, the authors train random forest models to predict LyC escape fraction and escape rate. They identify SFR ratios and gas-to-stellar mass as key diagnostics for f_esc, and M_UV for escape rate. Using UV luminosity functions, they construct reionization histories consistent with observations, finding reionization occurred rapidly after z≈8 driven by UV-bright galaxies.
AI.motivation: To resolve the major uncertainty of how Lyman-continuum photons escape from early galaxies and to address the recently reported crisis in the ionizing photon budget of cosmic reionization.
AI.method: Analyzed >35,000 galaxy realizations from THESAN-ZOOM cosmological radiation-hydrodynamic simulations (z=3-16); trained random forest regression models using indirect diagnostics; constructed reionization histories from observed UV luminosity functions combined with derived M_UV–escape rate relations.
AI.result: The SFR_10/SFR_100 ratio and gas-to-stellar mass ratio are strongest predictors of f_esc; M_UV dominates prediction of escape rate; reionization histories from UV luminosity functions are consistent with observations, avoiding the ionizing photon budget crisis.
AI.conclusion: Bulk of reionization occurred rapidly after z≈8, driven by UV-bright galaxies with M_UV<-17 providing the dominant contribution.
